key_insight: Entrance-induced vortices create geometry-specific temperature-polarization bias whose magnitude and direction change with inlet Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: Lab-scale membrane characterization and heat-transfer correlations should account for inlet geometry and operating conditions rather than apply a constant entrance correction.
method: Three-dimensional CFD of direct contact membrane distillation.
Varied side-chamber length and main-channel height.
evidence_signal: Simulations found entrance vortices in all geometries, with greater downstream persistence at higher Reynolds numbers and, for most geometries, a shift from stronger to weaker temperature polarization relative to a straight-channel baseline.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational results without experimental validation; applicability beyond the simulated geometries and conditions requires testing.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
